model.name: Model for talinolol absorption and secretion in the intestine

notes.body:
Model for talinolol absorption and secretion in the intestine
The intestine is a tube of six segments (duodenum, two jejunum, two ileum segments and the colon), each a lumen with its enterocytes. The oral dose dissolves into the duodenum (dissolution_tal), the lumen is transported from segment to segment (TALFLUX_*, a transit of about 4.7 hr through the small intestine and 22.5 hr through the colon) and leaves the colon into the feces (TALEXC).
Talinolol, a hydrophilic beta blocker, is taken up into the enterocytes with a first order (TALABS_*, passive and OATP2B1) and pumped back into the lumen by P-glycoprotein (TALEFL_*), whose amount increases along the small intestine (pgp_*). The efflux saturates (TALEFL_Km), so that the bioavailability increases with the dose (the AUC per mg rises 1.8 fold from 25 to 400 mg, DeMey1995; Wetterich1996, Siegmund2003). The basolateral membrane is passed in both directions (TALEX_*): the enterocytes take up talinolol from the plasma of the gut as well, and P-glycoprotein secretes it into the lumen against the gradient, the main nonrenal elimination of talinolol after an intravenous dose (Gramatte1996, Westphal2000a/b, Bernsdorf2006: an intestinal clearance of about 74 ml/min), which an inducer (rifampicin) increases after an intravenous dose as well.
The content of this model has been carefully created in a manual research effort.

parameter.name: rate of the apical uptake of talinolol

body.p: The apical uptake of talinolol into the enterocytes is of first order, oatp2b1_<segment> * TALABS_k * Vgu * [talinolol lumen]: passive and by OATP2B1. Talinolol is a substrate of OATP2B1 (Km = 459 ± 260 µmol/l, Roustom2017), but the uptake does not saturate in vivo, the bioavailability increases with the dose.
The value of GU__TALABS_k is the result of the fit PK_20261020_042735__49b48, its uncertainty is the profile likelihood of the fit.

parameter.name: Km of the efflux of talinolol by P-glycoprotein

body.p: The efflux of talinolol by P-glycoprotein saturates at the concentrations in the enterocytes after the higher oral doses, so that the bioavailability increases with the dose (DeMey1995: the AUC per mg rises 1.8 fold from 25 to 400 mg; Siegmund2003: "first order nonionic diffusion diminished by ... saturated P-gp"). It is an apparent value of the concentration in the enterocytes of the model, whose volume is assumed (a tenth of the lumen).
The value of GU__TALEFL_Km is the result of the fit PK_20261020_042735__49b48, its uncertainty is the profile likelihood of the fit.

parameter.name: rate of the basolateral transport of talinolol

body.p: The basolateral transport between the enterocytes and the plasma of the intestine is passive in both directions, driven by the unbound concentration in the plasma: TALEX_k * Vgu * ([talinolol enterocytes] - fup_tal * [talinolol plasma]).
parameter controls velocity (1.0 reference velocity, < 1.0 reduced velocity, > 1.0 increased velocity)
parameter controls activity (1.0 reference activity, < 1.0 reduced activity, > 1.0 increased activity)
